carousels.name: 4 risk factors when casual p*rn use becomes addiction (1 in 13)

slides.title: 4 risk factors that turn casual p*rn use [[into addiction.]]
slides.sub: 56.7% had watched. About 1 in 13 screened positive for addiction.

slides.title: Screened [[positive]]
slides.body: In a survey of 1,008 young adults in Rhode Island (2024 data, published 2025), 56.7% had viewed p*rn and 7.9% — about 1 in 13 — screened positive for p*rn addiction.

slides.title: Risks [[1–2]]
items: Using it to cope — stress, loneliness, bad moods.
Starting young — research links earlier exposure to more compulsive use.

slides.title: Risks [[3–4]]
items: Binges and escalation — longer sessions, more extreme content.
Secrecy — when nobody knows, nothing pushes back.

slides.title: Check [[yourself]]
items: Ask: do I watch p*rn to feel better?
Notice if sessions are getting longer.
Tell one person — secrecy feeds it.
Get help early — it's easier than later.

carousels.name: 5 things therapy for p*rn addiction actually involves

slides.title: 5 things therapy for p*rn addiction [[actually involves.]]
slides.sub: It's less scary than you think.

slides.title: You [[talk]], they listen
slides.body: No lecture. No shock. A good therapist has heard it before. You can describe your p*rn use without graphic details.

slides.title: You find the [[why]]
slides.body: Stress, loneliness, old habits — therapy looks at what p*rn is doing for you. That's where lasting change starts.

slides.title: Things [[3–5]]
items: Practical tools — for example, CBT skills for handling urges.
Homework — small changes to try between sessions.
Often online — from your own room, on your schedule.

slides.title: How to [[start]]
items: Look for a therapist who works with compulsive sexual behavior.
Ask about online sessions if in-person feels hard.
Say it plainly in session one: "I struggle with p*rn."
Give it 3 sessions before deciding.

carousels.name: 4 excuses that sound mature but keep you watching p*rn

slides.title: 4 excuses that sound mature [[but keep you watching p*rn.]]
"I'm an adult. [[It's my choice.]]"
slides.body: Sure. Then make one. Is it a choice if you can't stop? Freedom includes saying no to p*rn.

slides.title: "It's [[better]] than cheating."
slides.body: Comparing it to something worse doesn't make it good. The bar isn't "not cheating."

slides.title: Excuses [[3–4]]
items: "It helps me sleep." So would a routine that doesn't leave you wired at 2 AM.
"Everything in moderation." Moderation you've tried 40 times isn't a plan.

slides.title: The grown-up [[move]]
items: Be honest about how much you actually watch.
Count the times you've tried to cut back.
Decide — quit p*rn, with a real plan.
Get support, like an adult would.
